author: Fred Pickhardt
title: Major Hurricane Lowell Update
text:
Hurricane Lowell has rapidly intensified into a dangerous Category 5 hurricane, packing maximum sustained winds of 140 knots (160 mph).
Current Status & Intensity
Location: Near 13.3N, 154.3W (as of 11:00 AM HST, Sept 2, 2026).
Movement: Moving just south of due west (265°) at 9 knots.
Structure: Extremely compact and highly symmetric. It features a warm, 15-nautical-mile-wide eye surrounded by deep convection.
Radius Hurricane Winds: 20-30 nm
Radius 50 knot Winds: 30-40 nm
Max Significant Wave Height: 14-15 meters (46-49 feet)
Potential: Near-term intensification is still possible due to low wind shear and warm ocean waters. It is forecast to peak around 145 knots in the next 12 hours and is highly confident to remain a major hurricane through the weekend.
Track Shift
Short-Term (Next 2–3 Days): Lowell will continue heading west-southwest at a gradually slowing forward speed, passing well south of the main Hawaiian Islands.
Long-Term (The Weekend & Beyond): An upper-level low dropping from the North Pacific will weaken the steering ridge. A sharp, dramatic turn toward the north or north-northeast is expected between days 4 and 5 (Sunday into Monday).
